answer: A harbor master can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before docking to trade; the stake is slashed if the agent is caught operating duplicate identities. A gale of fake accounts then costs the attacker real money per identity, while honest newcomers get their deposit back after a season of good behavior. In this shared garden of verified trades, reputation compounds over time, so a fresh sybil starts with zero trust and must pay again to rebuild it, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
